title: Investigate trailing delimiter introduced in customer evaluations after sampling defaults change
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Several customers reported reproducible evaluation failures and unexpected trailing text in JSON-structured eval outputs after a recent change to the platform's sampling defaults. Problem was first reported by ClearLedger on Hosted (support ticket #54721) and later reproduced against a Dedicated pool and one Private deployment clone. Symptoms include an extra invisible delimiter or short phrase appended to otherwise-parsable JSON outputs, causing downstream evaluation scripts to fail strict parsing checks. This ticket contains the investigation, root cause, fix plan, rollout, QA, and customer comms.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use Redwood hosted text generation endpoint with model=rw-medium-1, sampling configuration set to default sampler (no explicit seed and default temperature).
2) POST prompt body containing a JSON schema anchor and an explicit end marker string (customer uses '<<END>>') and request deterministic-ish eval via low temperature (0.2).

3) Observe generated payload: top-level JSON is present but contains a trailing two-character delimiter (​ or a short phrase 'END
') appended after the closing brace, causing JSON.parse to throw in strict eval harnesses.

4) Reproduce on Dedicated pool and Private VPC with same model and runtime version; behaviour observed when runtime sampling defaults are active and when prefix merging is triggered by routing overlays.
investigation_notes: 2026-02-25 - Asha: Triage call with support; ClearLedger supplied 3 failing eval prompt payloads. Repro locally with hosted token. Assigned to Diego.
2026-02-26 - Diego: Reproduced on local dev cluster when 'prefix-merge' codepath runs with 'normalize-sampling-anchors' flag enabled. Observed invisible U+200B zero-width space in merged prompt tail.

2026-02-27 - Lina: Traced insertion point to sampler-defaults normalization pass introduced in runtime-1.22.0 config. The normalization adds a delimiter to separate prompt segments when prefix merging could drop explicit terminators in some routing fallthrough cases.

2026-02-28 - Samir: Verified that explicit customer end-markers are being preserved in most flows, but in the presence of prefix-level routing overrides the normalization pass injects a zero-width separator which surfaces as trailing characters after tokenization and detokenization for some tokenizer variants.
2026-03-01 - Diego: Unit tests show that the invisible delimiter is preserved through KV cache boundary and is not removed by final output post-processing due to a regression in 'trim-anchors' logic.
root_cause: A normalization change in the sampling-defaults merge step (runtime-1.22.0) inserted a zero-width separator to avoid accidental token concatenation during prefix merging. In certain routing overlays and when customers supply explicit end markers, the separator remained in the final output because the trimming logic failed to recognize the invisible character. This caused well-formed JSON outputs to have a trailing invisible character or a short appended phrase in a small fraction of requests, breaking strict eval parsers.
fix_summary: 1) Adjust prefix-merge normalization to avoid inserting invisible separators when an explicit end marker is present. 2) Harden trim-anchors post-processing to normalize and remove known invisible separator codepoints (e.g., U+200B) and short injected phrases when they appear after explicit terminators. 3) Add end-to-end tests covering hosted/dedicated/private flows including tokenizer round-trip and KV cache boundaries. 4) Add an opt-in compatibility toggle for customers who want pre-change behavior.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement fix and unit tests on branch fix/eng-121734-delim-cleanup.
2) Run integration tests against staging clusters for hosted, dedicated, and private runtime images (runtime-1.22.1 candidate).
3) Canary deploy to 1% of hosted traffic and smoke test ClearLedger's failing prompts in a seeded repro harness.
4) If green after 24h, expand to 10% then 50% and full rollout in 48h increments. For Dedicated/Private customers coordinate with account owners for maintenance windows.
5) Provide immediate rollback plan: revert normalization change or toggle compatibility flag per-customer if severe regressions observed.
qa_plan: - Add unit tests that assert no invisible separators are present when explicit end markers exist.
- Add integration tests that post-process outputs through customer's strict JSON parsers (sample harness from ClearLedger).
- Run tokenizer round-trip tests across supported tokenizer versions to ensure zero-width characters are removed prior to final serialization.
- Manual verification: run ClearLedger prompt set against canary and compare eval pass rate before/after fix.
customer_communication: Initial ack: 2026-02-25 - Support sent standard ack and opened ticket; engineering engaged.

Escalation update: 2026-03-02 - Told ClearLedger we identified a root cause in sampling-defaults normalization and are preparing a targeted fix. Offered a temporary mitigation: set explicit sampling configuration (disable normalization) or use the compatibility flag once available.

Post-fix plan: Notify ClearLedger and affected customers when canary passes with instructions to validate eval harnesses. Provide compensated support hours and review any broken runs for re-evaluation.
